region: Capital city in Democratic Republic of the Congo
heroText: Kinshasa is the sprawling capital of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, facing Brazzaville across the wide Congo River. First-time visitors should tour the Musée National de la RDC for Congolese art and history, browse the Grand Marché for textiles and crafts, and walk the Boulevard du 30 Juin through the government district. N'djili International Airport connects Kinshasa to the rest of Africa and beyond.

areas.name: Gombe
areas.text: Gombe is Kinshasa's central district of embassies, government offices and the capital's priciest hotels, the most convenient base for first-time visitors.

areas.name: Limete
areas.text: Limete blends a modern city feel with civic buildings and educational institutions, a practical option for business travellers and longer stays.

areas.name: Bandalungwa (Bandal)
areas.text: Bandalungwa is a busy, more local residential district, useful for travellers wanting an authentic slice of everyday Kinshasa life.

airports.name: N'djili International Airport (FIH)
airports.search: N'djili International Airport, Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo
airports.text: N'djili International Airport lies east of the city centre; traffic on the route into Gombe can be heavy, so build in extra time.

airportTransfer.value: Compare road transfer time between N'djili International Airport (FIH) and central Kinshasa before choosing an airport-area or city-centre hotel.

bookingDestination: Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo
stayOverview: Base in Gombe for a secure, central first stay near embassies, hotels and government offices, or choose Limete for a more business-focused, longer stay. Bandalungwa suits travellers wanting a livelier, more local base.
hotelIntro: Kinshasa hotel choice usually follows budget and purpose: Gombe holds the capital's international hotel brands and safest central streets, Limete offers a modern, business-friendly alternative, and Bandalungwa provides more affordable, local-feeling options.
rentalCars: Self-drive car rental isn't recommended given Kinshasa's dense traffic; arrange a hotel driver or trusted taxi service instead.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Choose Gombe for a secure, central stay close to embassies, hotels and the Musée National de la RDC.

travelTips.title: Traffic and transfers
travelTips.text: Budget extra time for Kinshasa's heavy traffic, especially between N'djili International Airport and central districts during peak hours.

travelTips.title: Cash and safety
travelTips.text: Carry Congolese francs and US dollars in small denominations, and keep valuables out of sight in busy markets and streets.

travelTips.title: River views
travelTips.text: Head to the Boulevard du 30 Juin riverside stretch for views across the Congo River toward Brazzaville on the opposite bank.

history.text: The city was established as a trading post by Henry Morton Stanley in 1881.
The completion of the Matadi–Kinshasa portage railway, in 1898, provided an alternative route around the rapids and sparked the rapid development of Léopoldville.
In 1914, a pipeline was installed so that crude oil could be transported from Matadi to the upriver steamers in Leopoldville.

By 1923, the city was elevated to capital of the Belgian Congo, replacing the town of Boma in the Congo estuary, pursuant to the Royal Decree of 1 July 1923, countersigned by the Minister of the Colonies, Louis Franc.
On 2 May 1966, the government announced that the nation's major cities would be restored to their pre-colonial names, effective on 30 June, the sixth anniversary of independence.
